title: Harmonic Drive gears: mechanism and component packages
creator: Harmonic Drive SE
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Separates the three-part reduction mechanism from component sets and units with output bearings.
first_task: Find the component-set and output-bearing categories, then list which housing and support work your joint still needs.
limitations: Commercial performance statements refer to engineered products, not generic or printed flexsplines.
evidence_note: Opened official overview; inspected wave generator, flexspline, circular spline, and the distinct package categories.

title: SHF and SHG engineering catalog
creator: Harmonic Drive LLC
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Shows that low backlash, loaded twist, efficiency, output support, and life are separate specification questions.
first_task: Inspect the torque-versus-twist curves and the separate backdriving and output-bearing sections.
limitations: A teaching example of catalog structure. Confirm the current catalog and limits for any actual purchased configuration; no part has been selected.
evidence_note: Opened the 59-page official PDF; confirmed separate ratings/life, assembly tolerance, output-bearing, efficiency, backdriving, torsional stiffness, and hysteresis sections.

title: Cycloidal gear technology
creator: Sumitomo Drive Technologies
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Names the eccentric, lobed disc, stationary outer pins, and output pins so the two pin sets are not confused.
first_task: Trace which pins stay fixed and which transmit the output, then predict rotation for a one-lobe difference.
limitations: One-stage examples require a specified fixed member and lobe difference. Product load and vibration claims do not rate a printed mechanism.
evidence_note: Opened official mechanism page and checked the input, disc, fixed ring, output extraction, and paired-disc discussion.

title: Cycloidal and strain-wave drives
creator: Jönköping University — Applied Mechanics
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Develops the signed ratios and explains why the cycloidal output holes must accommodate eccentricity.
first_task: Check the ratio for eleven fixed pins and ten lobes; identify the output-hole enlargement.
limitations: Geometry and teaching examples do not provide a physical rating for the guide’s schematics or your print.
evidence_note: Opened university chapter and inspected the fixed-ring ratio derivation and output-hole explanation.

title: Herringbone gears
creator: Jönköping University — Applied Mechanics
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Connects tooth helix angle to axial force and the use of opposite-handed halves.
first_task: Sketch the axial force directions for a single helix and then for opposed helices.
limitations: Ideal thrust cancellation does not remove the need to assess unequal loading, manufacturing error, and retention. The guide does not adopt a universal printed-gear recommendation.
evidence_note: Opened university chapter; inspected the helix-angle force relation and opposite-hand construction.

title: Bevel gears
creator: Jönköping University — Applied Mechanics
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Explains how intersecting shaft axes and the gear forces constrain the supporting structure.
first_task: Locate the pitch-cone intersection and mark axial forces before drawing a housing.
limitations: The guide uses only the arrangement and support principles; its pivot is not a designed bevel-gear assembly.
evidence_note: Opened university chapter; inspected pitch cones, shaft angles, force components, and mounting sections.

title: Why lead screws fit many linear-motion applications
creator: Thomson
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Explains how sliding friction, nut materials, duty, and wear enter screw selection.
first_task: Compare a short intermittent move with continuous reciprocation at the same force.
limitations: Numerical product ranges and historical cost examples are not universal limits. Obtain the chosen screw/nut specifications.
evidence_note: Opened official technical article; inspected friction/efficiency, backdriving, critical speed, duty, backlash, wear, and lubrication.

title: Selecting the optimal screw technology
creator: Tolomatic
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Distinguishes sliding threads, recirculating balls, and threaded rollers, with different cost and integration constraints.
first_task: Identify the load-carrying contact in each screw type and the power-off behavior of a vertical axis.
limitations: Manufacturer comparisons need application-specific ratings and total package cost; the guide does not transfer a family’s performance claims to arbitrary products.
evidence_note: Opened official article; inspected operating principles and selection tradeoffs for Acme, ball, and planetary roller screws.

title: The Complete Guide to Chain
creator: U.S. Tsubaki / Tsubakimoto Chain Co.
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Shows why a chain’s discrete pitch produces cyclic speed variation around a sprocket.
first_task: Read section 2.2.1 and compare small and large sprocket tooth counts.
limitations: The archived textbook explains principles; current drive selection, lubrication, and maintenance limits require the actual chain documentation.
evidence_note: Opened official hosted book and inspected section 2.2.1, including the maximum/minimum chain-speed explanation.

title: Chain wear guide instructions
creator: Renold
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Makes wear elongation a measurable maintenance condition rather than an assumed fixed clearance.
first_task: Identify what length is being measured and why worn sprockets and chain need joint inspection.
limitations: Replacement thresholds are those of the referenced guide, not a universal criterion for every precision robot transmission.
evidence_note: Read official indexed PDF text describing elongation assessment and replacement guidance.

title: Transmissions and guides
creator: MIT Center for Bits and Atoms — Machine Class
prerequisites: Motor versus transmission, reduction ratio, and basic force/torque concepts
access: Free public source; linked documents remain on the creator’s site.
why: Explains cable wrap, termination, and alignment considerations in a capstan transmission.
first_task: Trace how wrap and maintained tension provide traction, then contrast that with a tendon fixed to a spool.
limitations: Course design notes are qualitative. Cable material, bend radius, traction, fatigue, stroke, and force capability require a specific design.
evidence_note: Opened course page; inspected capstan wrap, helical cable travel, positive preload, termination, and manufacturing comments.
